scope: Pause/resume ordering, timeout suspension, retries and pending intents under concurrent operations (src/coordinator.ts, src/store.ts, src/domain.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/providers/opencode.ts)

findings.title: Control intent recorded during an in-flight step is applied after that step settles the worker, regressing a terminal state to paused
findings.evidence: runControl (src/coordinator.ts:833-834) stores the intent durably then calls exclusive(id, step); exclusive (:251-257) returns the in-flight step promise, so the control never runs its own step. store.finish (src/store.ts:291) and the settled fail transition (src/coordinator.ts:800-804) leave w.intent set, and runTick (:345) admits any worker with an intent regardless of state, so applyControl (:837-856) pauses an already-terminal worker. Reproduced: state regressed completed -> paused with previous_state 'completed' (events worker.completed -> worker.paused) and recovery_required -> paused with previous_state 'recovery_required'.
findings.reproduction: tests/helpers.ts doubles only. /tmp/rev-scope/probe/pause-race.test.ts PROBE 1: run to running, agent.complete, gate agent.inspect mid-monitor(), call control(id,'pause') while the step holds the lock, release. Output: after completion {state:completed,intent:pause}, after one tick {state:paused,previous_state:completed}; a follow-up message is answered {state:paused,delivery:queued} and stays dispatch state 'pending' with submitted still 1 after two more ticks. PROBE 2: same race with no reply, so the in-flight monitor fails the worker as ambiguous delivery -> {state:recovery_required,intent:pause} then {state:paused,previous_state:recovery_required}. Real window: agent.inspect (2 guest calls, 30s bound each) and pushBranch (120s bound).
findings.recommendation: Do not let an intent survive a terminal transition: re-validate in step before applyControl (only cancel/destroy should act on terminal states) and clear intent in store.finish and in fail's settled transitions, so a stale intent cannot regress completed/recovery_required to paused. Report the resulting state to the caller instead of silently regressing.

findings.title: Follow-up queued while a paused worker holds a terminal previous_state inflates the post-resume provisioning window by up to the pause duration
findings.evidence: queueMessage stamps provision_started_at: Date.now() (src/coordinator.ts:235) while the worker is paused, and applyControl resume then adds elapsed = Date.now() - paused_at to that stamp (:863-865), double counting the already-elapsed part of the pause. The boot guard at src/coordinator.ts:444-451 (SWARMFORGE_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300) therefore cannot fire for that duration.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev-scope/probe/provision-window.test.ts PROBE 3: complete the worker, pause it, set paused_at 1h in the past, send a follow-up, resume. Output: after message {state:paused,previous_state:ready,provision_started_at_in:0}; after resume {state:ready,provision_started_at_in_s:3600,boot_window_remaining_s:3900} instead of the configured 300s.
findings.recommendation: Do not overwrite provision_started_at with Date.now() in queueMessage while paused, or clamp the resume shift to the time actually elapsed since the stamp, so the configured provision window is not silently extended.
